subject: Urgent: Acme reserved capacity gap impacting P95 latency — immediate mitigation request
messages:

Subject: Production: reserved capacity not meeting committed throughput (urgent)

Hannah / Marissa —

We’re seeing sustained P95 latency spikes and token-rate throttling on our dedicated pool for the last 45 minutes. Dashboard shows sustained queueing and a rise in 5xx error rates. This is impacting live inference for two payment flows (visible in trace IDs below).

Quick summary:
- Observed: P95 latency jumped from ~280ms to ~1.2s and token throughput is ~55% of our committed rate for the pool.
- Errors: 5xx on ~2.1% of calls (spike from baseline ~0.03%).
- Scope: All regions routed to the reserved pool for account ACME-7891.

We need an immediate mitigation timeline and a plan for full throughput recovery. This is causing transaction backlogs and merchant-facing timeouts. Please treat as Sev2->1 if this looks systemic.

I attached the raw metrics export.

Attachments: [acme-prod-metrics-2027-03-30.csv]

Thanks,
David
Senior Ops Engineer, Acme Corp

3) We’ll provide an ETA for full recovery and a remediation plan within 45 minutes.

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme reserved pool triage + quick decision needed

Team — copying internal only for quick triage (David and Marissa already looped on public reply). Key asks:

- Confirm if this is pool saturation vs model/regression. Quick checks: GPU utilization per node, queue length distribution, recent kernel rollout (past 48h), and routing policy changes.
- If pool saturation, can we: 1) spin up 4 burst nodes into the dedicated pool? 2) move Acme to a higher-IO model variant (compatibility ok for 2 hours)?
- Cost/time tradeoff: need an ETA that we can send to the customer (30m, 60m, 2h).

I’ve attached the pool usage snapshot from monitoring (pulled at 09:28).

Attachments: [pool-usage-snapshot.txt]

Hannah
(If we escalate, I’ll mark for exec readout and include Marissa.)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme reserved pool triage + quick decision needed

Hannah — quick triage results:

- Evidence points to pool-level saturation: multiple nodes at pinned 98–100% GPU util; queue depth concentrated on Acme routing shards. No recent kernel rollout matching the timing.
- Root cause hypothesis: burst of long-context requests + suboptimal batching from Acme's recent client-side change (we see larger-than-expected sequence lengths).

Short-term plan (ETA and impact):
1) Immediate: spin up 4 burst GPU nodes into ACME pool — ETA ~22–30 minutes to be traffic-ready. Restores estimated throughput to ~95% of committed. (Cost: estimated additional $1.2k/hr)
2) Canary: move 10% of traffic to the higher-IO variant with prefix caching enabled — ETA for canary config ~35 minutes. Will monitor 1m/5m P95.
3) Medium: request Acme to reduce client-side batch windows (config change) — ask already sent by Hannah.
4) If customer approves, sales can offer a one-time credit for the hour-overage while we stabilize; Marissa to confirm.

I’ll prepare a short canary plan and a rollback path. Opening internal ticket: SUP-4321. Attaching draft canary plan.

Attachments: [canary-plan.md]

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

David — quick update and proposed immediate plan: 

1) We will spin up 4 burst nodes into your dedicated pool now (ETA 25–30 minutes). This should get you back to ~90–95% of committed throughput while we stabilize.
2) We’ll run a 10% canary on a higher-IO variant with prefix caching for critical routes — monitoring windows at 1m/5m to validate P95 improvements.
3) Expected customer impact: latency should fall back toward baseline within ~35–45 minutes; token throughput should materially recover within the same window.
4) Cost & credits: temporary bump will incur extra hourly cost; Marissa is able to confirm a one-time credit to offset this (pending your approval).

Please reply with an explicit ok to proceed with the temporary capacity bump and canary. If we don’t hear back within 10 minutes we’ll proceed with the burst nodes and notify you as they come online.
